findings.rationale: Folded Phase 2 Requests: per request id per-counter max with the stored max kept (idempotent for repeated lines, split responses and rereads); spike on 12 503 real requests found identical usage on every line; fixtures listed.
Folded Phase 2 store: dir 0700, db create-or-tighten 0600, existing -wal/-shm tightened, only then open; test from a 0644 db with a stale 0644 -wal.

Folded Phase 3: value constraints for every string (alias grammar, host, model regex with unknown fallback at collect time, day, enums, numbers); push refuses otherwise; tests put a path and an email into model and alias.

Folded Phase 2 Account of a root: collect never reads AUTOPILOT_ACCOUNT; snapshots carry root = sha8(canonical config dir); a root maps to the newest matching snapshot alias else acct-sha8, stored in the db.
Folded Phase 1: exact snapshot keys and the only statusline input read (rate_limits.*); privacy test on snapshot bytes with markers in session_id, transcript_path, cwd, workspace.
Same fold as 965bcf2f, plus: lines without requestId skipped; missing cache_creation breakdown falls back to cache_creation_input_tokens as 5-minute writes.
Folded Phase 2 Incremental: head = sha256 of the first min(4096, committed offset) bytes with that length, compared over the same length only.
Same fold as 911b1142, plus upload with a fixed --name so no local path is sent, tested with a fake fleet recording argv and bytes; summary.json location stated.
Folded Phase 1 read rule: file stem must equal the body alias and match the grammar (implemented in phase 2 with a negative test).
Folded Phase 3: per-model rate rows written out (no rule-plus-exception path), tests pin the read exceptions; totals sum priced rows with an explicit partial marker, null when none priced.

Folded Phase 1 row rule: whole entry, or alias NN% without countdown, or omitted, never cut mid-token; most constrained kept first; red never demoted. Matches the implementation reviewed SHIP-AS-IS (f6baef59).
Folded criterion 5: G36-owned dirs only, <data_dir>/usage/ via CODEFORGE_DATA_DIR (as src/db) for usage.db and <live_base>/codeforge/usage/ for quota and summary.json; ~/.codeforge is not touched.
